evals.prompt: One of my jobs has been (Priority) for an hour. Another just went to QOSMaxCpuPerJobLimit and I always submit with -q public. What's happening and what do I do?
evals.expected_output: (Priority) is normal fairshare queueing (backfill / smaller job starts sooner). QOSMaxCpuPerJobLimit cannot be a real -q public per-job cap (public has none), so the job is on debug/class/a typo'd QoS or it's really QOSMaxCpuPerUserLimit; confirm with scontrol show job / sacctmgr show qos, then resubmit on -q public. No script, no submission.
assertions: Explains (Priority) as normal fairshare queueing behind higher-priority work, not an error; mentions backfill or that a smaller/shorter job starts sooner.
Recognizes that -q public has no per-job CPU cap, so QOSMaxCpuPerJobLimit means the job is not really on -q public (leftover -q debug, a class QoS, or a typo) or is actually the PerUser variant.
Recommends confirming with `scontrol show job <id>` (QOS= field) and/or `sacctmgr show qos` before acting.
Recommended fix is to put the job back on -q public and resubmit; does not over-promise an in-place `scontrol update ... QOS=` change (or notes it may be denied).
Writes no batch script and submits/modifies no real job.
